papers.title: Graph Learning-Driven Multi-Vessel Association: Fusing Multimodal Data for Maritime Intelligence
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
papers.abstract: Ensuring maritime safety and optimizing traffic management in increasingly crowded and complex waterways require effective waterway monitoring. However, current methods struggle with challenges arising from multimodal data, such as dimensional disparities, mismatched target counts, vessel scale variations, occlusions, and asynchronous data streams from systems like the automatic identification system (AIS) and closed-circuit television (CCTV). Traditional multi-vessel association methods often struggle with these complexities, particularly in densely trafficked waterways. To overcome these issues, we propose a graph learning-driven multi-vessel association (named GMvA) method tailored for maritime multimodal data fusion. By integrating AIS and CCTV data, GMvA leverages time series learning and graph neural networks to capture the spatiotemporal features of vessel trajectories effectively. To enhance feature representation, the proposed method incorporates temporal graph attention and spatiotemporal attention, effectively capturing both local and global vessel interactions. Furthermore, a multi-layer perceptron-based uncertainty fusion module computes robust similarity scores, and the Hungarian algorithm is adopted to ensure globally consistent and accurate target matching. To validate the efficacy of our method, we have also constructed a new maritime multimodal dataset (termed MaritimeMmD) for data fusion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GMvA delivers superior accuracy and robustness in multi-vessel association, outperforming existing methods even in challenging scenarios with high vessel density and incomplete or unevenly distributed AIS and CCTV data. The source dataset and code are available athttps://github.com/LouisYxLu/GMvA

papers.abstract_zh: 在日益拥挤和复杂的水道中保障海上安全并优化交通管理，需要有效的水道监测。然而，当前方法难以应对多模态数据带来的挑战，例如维度差异、目标数量不匹配、船舶尺度变化、遮挡，以及来自自动识别系统（AIS）和闭路电视（CCTV）等系统的异步数据流。传统多船关联方法往往难以处理这些复杂性，尤其是在交通密集的水道中。为克服这些问题，我们提出一种面向海上多模态数据融合的图学习驱动多船关联方法（称为GMvA）。通过整合AIS和CCTV数据，GMvA利用时间序列学习和图神经网络有效捕捉船舶轨迹的时空特征。为增强特征表示，所提方法引入时间图注意力和时空注意力，有效捕捉船舶的局部和全局交互。此外，基于多层感知机的不确定性融合模块计算稳健的相似度得分，并采用匈牙利算法确保全局一致且准确的目标匹配。为验证方法的有效性，我们还构建了一个用于数据融合的新海上多模态数据集（称为MaritimeMmD）。大量实验表明，GMvA在多船关联中具有更高的准确性和鲁棒性，即使在船舶密度高且AIS和CCTV数据不完整或分布不均的挑战性场景中也优于现有方法。源数据集和代码可在https://github.com/LouisYxLu/GMvA获取。

papers.title: CLLAP: Contrastive Learning-based LiDAR-Augmented Pretraining for Enhanced Radar-Camera Fusion
papers.abstract: Accurate 3D object detection is critical for autonomous driving, necessitating reliable, cost-effective sensors capable of operating in adverse weather conditions. Camera and millimeter-wave radar fusion has emerged as a promising solution; however, these methods often rely on finely annotated radar data, which is scarce and labor-intensive to produce. To address this challenge, we present CLLAP, a Contrastive Learning-based LiDAR-Augmented Pretraining framework that enhances the performance of existing radar-camera fusion methods for 3D object detection. CLLAP leverages abundant LiDAR data to generate pseudo-radar data using the proposed L2R (LiDAR-to-Radar) Sampling method. Then, it incorporates this data into a novel dual-stage, dual-modality contrastive learning strategy, enabling effective self-supervised learning from paired pseudo-radar and image data. This approach facilitates effective pretraining of existing radar-camera fusion models in a plug-and-play manner, enhancing their feature extraction capabilities and improving detection accuracy and robustness. Experimental results using NuScenes and Lyft Level 5 datasets demonstrate significant performance improvements across three baseline models, highlighting CLLAP's effectiveness in advancing radar-camera fusion for autonomous driving applications.

papers.abstract_zh: 准确的3D目标检测对自动驾驶至关重要，需要可靠、低成本且能在恶劣天气条件下工作的传感器。相机与毫米波雷达融合已成为一种有前景的解决方案；然而，这些方法通常依赖精细标注的雷达数据，而此类数据稀缺且标注劳动强度大。为应对这一挑战，我们提出CLLAP，一种基于对比学习的LiDAR增强预训练框架，可提升现有雷达-相机融合方法在3D目标检测中的性能。CLLAP利用丰富的LiDAR数据，通过所提出的L2R（LiDAR-to-Radar）采样方法生成伪雷达数据。然后，它将这些数据纳入一种新颖的双阶段、双模态对比学习策略，从而能够从配对的伪雷达与图像数据中进行有效的自监督学习。该方法以即插即用的方式促进现有雷达-相机融合模型的有效预训练，增强其特征提取能力并提高检测精度与鲁棒性。使用NuScenes和Lyft Level 5数据集的实验结果表明，三个基线模型均取得显著的性能提升，凸显了CLLAP在推进自动驾驶雷达-相机融合方面的有效性。

papers.title: Towards Accurate 3D Object Detection in Adverse Weather by Leveraging 4D Radar for LiDAR Geometry Enhancement
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: 3D object detection is a critical component of autonomous driving, yet its performance degrades severely in adverse weather due to the degradation of LiDAR point clouds. While existing LiDAR-4D radar fusion methods enhance robustness by incorporating weather-robust 4D radar data, they often depend on well geometric structures from LiDAR and so struggle to effectively exploit radar data in case of degraded LiDAR data. To tackle this challenge, we propose REL, a novel 4D radar-guided LiDAR geometric enhancement framework. It utilizes 4D radar features to dynamically generate virtual LiDAR points, effectively increasing the density of degraded LiDAR data. Moreover, a Position-Guided Cross Attention (PGCA) module is proposed to enhance the feature representation of virtual points, while an Adaptive Feature Fusion (AFF) module is designed to integrate virtual and real LiDAR features. Extensive experiments on the K-Radar and Vod-Fog datasets demonstrate that REL achieves state-of-the-art 3D object detection performance under diverse adverse weather conditions. Notably, REL improves the overall AP3D by 9.3% on K-Radar and boosts the cyclist class by up to 52.9% 3D mAP under the most severe foggy condition on Vod-Fog.

papers.abstract_zh: 3D目标检测是自动驾驶的关键组成部分，然而在恶劣天气下，由于LiDAR点云退化，其性能会严重下降。现有LiDAR-4D Radar融合方法通过引入对天气鲁棒的4D Radar数据来增强鲁棒性，但它们往往依赖LiDAR良好的几何结构，因而在LiDAR数据退化时难以有效利用Radar数据。为应对这一挑战，我们提出REL，一种新颖的4D Radar引导的LiDAR几何增强框架。它利用4D Radar特征动态生成虚拟LiDAR点，有效提高退化LiDAR数据的密度。此外，提出位置引导交叉注意力（PGCA）模块以增强虚拟点的特征表示，并设计自适应特征融合（AFF）模块以整合虚拟与真实LiDAR特征。在K-Radar和Vod-Fog数据集上的大量实验表明，REL在多种恶劣天气条件下取得了最先进的3D目标检测性能。值得注意的是，REL在K-Radar上将整体AP3D提升9.3%，并在Vod-Fog最严重雾天条件下将骑行者类别的3D mAP最高提升52.9%。

papers.title: ATN3D: Density-Aware LiDAR-Radar Early 3D Object Detection Under Extreme Sparsity
papers.abstract: 3D object detection is the backbone of perception for automated vehicles (AV) and broader intelligent transportation systems applications. Long-range detection is challenging because sensing evidence is sparse; yet this ``long-range'' scenario is routine in traffic. Although >30m is often labeled long-range in computer vision, on roadways it affords only approx. 1-2s for perception and decision-making. Under such extreme sparsity, two core challenges arise. First, early multimodal fusion tends to discard sparsity information and inject noise from empty or falsely occupied cells, degrading long-range recall. Second, context-agnostic uniform channel supervision favors dense and near-range samples, leaving far and small objects under-optimized, delaying the earliest detection of distant objects. We propose ``Ask The Neighbor'' (ATN3D), a LiDAR-Radar framework tailored for sparse-range conditions. ATN3D introduces (i) Density-aware early fusion with cross-modal gating that conditions fusion on per-voxel density/sparsity and Radar evidence, (ii) Occupancy-gated neighborhood aggregation with circular kernels to aggregate only from credible cells, (iii) Evidence-conditioned channel self-attention to adapt channel weights with weather/range, and (iv) a Range-aware loss that re-balances classification and localization by distance, aligning training with distance-stratified evaluation. On the VoD benchmark across clear and foggy conditions, ATN3D surpasses strong baselines: +3.55% mAP in clear weather and +8.41% mAP under simulated heavy fog; for >30m objects, gains are +3.33% (clear) and +2.09% (heavy fog). These results indicate earlier and more reliable long-range detections under sparse sensing in on-road traffic.

papers.abstract_zh: 3D目标检测是自动驾驶汽车（AV）及更广泛智能交通系统应用感知的骨干。远距离检测具有挑战性，因为传感证据稀疏；然而这种“远距离”场景在交通中是常态。尽管在计算机视觉中超过30m常被标为远距离，在道路上它仅提供约1-2s的感知与决策时间。在这种极端稀疏下，出现两个核心挑战。第一，早期多模态融合倾向于丢弃稀疏信息，并从空或虚假占用单元注入噪声，降低远距离召回。第二，上下文无关的均匀通道监督偏向密集和近距样本，使远距和小目标优化不足，延迟对远处目标的最早检测。我们提出“Ask The Neighbor”（ATN3D），一个面向稀疏距离条件的LiDAR-Radar框架。ATN3D引入（i）密度感知早期融合与跨模态门控，以逐体素密度/稀疏度和Radar证据为条件进行融合，（ii）占用门控邻域聚合与圆形核，仅从可信单元聚合，（iii）证据条件通道自注意力，随天气/距离自适应通道权重，以及（iv）距离感知损失，按距离重新平衡分类与定位，使训练与距离分层评估对齐。在VoD基准的晴天和雾天条件下，ATN3D超越强基线：晴天mAP +3.55%，模拟浓雾下mAP +8.41%；对于>30m目标，增益为+3.33%（晴天）和+2.09%（浓雾）。这些结果表明在道路上稀疏传感下更早、更可靠的远距离检测。

papers.title: Do Pretrained Backbones Transfer to Physical Sensors? A Systematic Study of Multimodal Initialization Across the Sensor Stack
papers.abstract: Transfer learning from pretrained backbones has become standard practice in multi-sensor computer vision---yet two questions remain open: which pretrained weights transfer best to multi-sensor setups, and can in-domain pretraining outperform off-the-shelf solutions? Frameworks like MultiMAE demonstrate the utility of masked autoencoding in a multi-modal context, but rely entirely on dense, model-derived modalities. It is unclear how robustly these methods translate to real-world applications that use physical sensors, where the aggregation of diverse public datasets for large-scale pretraining inherently introduces modality sparsity. To investigate this systematically, we curate a multi-sensor autonomous driving collection of $2.82M$ images from 16 publicly available datasets, incorporating both physical hardware modalities (RGB, LWIR, NIR, Event) and model-derived modalities (Stereo Depth, Segmentation). We use this collection for in-domain pretraining based on the MultiMAE approach. We adapt MultiMAE's loss formulation to accommodate sparse samples, and study the effect of an enforced encoder bottleneck for modality alignment and of additional losses specific to dense reconstruction (SSIM and FFT). We then systematically compare against common pretrained backbones (ViT, MAE, DINO and MultiMAE) across downstream sensor fusion tasks. We find that MultiMAE is a surprisingly strong out-of-the-box baseline, transferring effectively even to modalities it has never seen, while our targeted modifications yield incremental but consistent improvements on multi-sensor transfer and overall robustness.

papers.abstract_zh: 从预训练骨干网络进行迁移学习已成为多传感器计算机视觉中的标准做法——然而两个问题仍未解决：哪些预训练权重最适合迁移到多传感器设置，以及域内预训练能否超越现成方案？像MultiMAE这样的框架展示了掩码自编码在多模态语境中的效用，但完全依赖稠密的、模型导出的模态。目前尚不清楚这些方法能多稳健地迁移到使用物理传感器的真实应用中，在这些应用中，为大规模预训练而聚合多样化的公开数据集会固有地引入模态稀疏性。为系统研究这一问题，我们整理了一个多传感器自动驾驶数据集，包含来自16个公开数据集的$2.82M$张图像，涵盖物理硬件模态（RGB、LWIR、NIR、Event）和模型导出模态（立体深度、分割）。我们使用该数据集基于MultiMAE方法进行域内预训练。我们调整MultiMAE的损失公式以适应稀疏样本，并研究强制编码器瓶颈对模态对齐的影响以及针对稠密重建的额外损失（SSIM和FFT）的影响。然后，我们在下游传感器融合任务中系统性地与常见预训练骨干网络（ViT、MAE、DINO和MultiMAE）进行比较。我们发现，MultiMAE是一个出乎意料的强大开箱即用基线，即使对从未见过的模态也能有效迁移，而我们针对性的修改在多传感器迁移和整体鲁棒性上带来了渐进但一致的改进。

reserve_papers.title: Perception-Aware Communication Middleware for Distributed Visual Perception in UAV Swarms
reserve_papers.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms increasingly support safety-critical applications that rely on distributed visual perception. Meeting the low-latency requirements of these applications can require perception models to execute within the swarm on inference-capable UAVs, creating a need for efficient UAV-to-UAV transport of high-bandwidth perception data. However, the Quality-of-Service (QoS) requirements of perception differ from conventional packet-level QoS; successful delivery of individual packets does not ensure that a complete, timely, and usable image is available for inference. We present a novel perception-aware communication middleware that treats complete perception-data samples as the communication objects for which QoS must be satisfied. The middleware extends a lightweight UDP broker-based publish-subscribe architecture with perception-specific services, including image fragmentation and reconstruction, concurrent packet transmission, priority-aware scheduling, and image quality assessment. The middleware is evaluated on a heterogeneous hardware testbed emulating a UAV swarm using YOLOv8n object detection. Experimental results demonstrate low end-to-end application latency, substantially higher throughput than a lightweight UDP broker, effective prioritization of perception traffic under increasing background load, and mitigation of object-detection degradation through middleware-level image quality assessment. This work provides an initial framework for integrating AI-specific data handling into communication middleware to support emerging distributed AI applications in multi-agent mobile cyber-physical systems.

reserve_papers.abstract_zh: 无人机（UAV）集群日益支撑依赖分布式视觉感知的安全关键应用。满足这些应用的低时延需求可能要求感知模型在集群内具备推理能力的UAV上执行，从而产生高效UAV到UAV传输高带宽感知数据的需要。然而，感知的服务质量（QoS）需求不同于传统包级QoS；单个数据包的成功交付并不保证有完整、及时且可用的图像可用于推理。我们提出一种新颖的感知感知通信中间件，将完整感知数据样本视为必须满足QoS的通信对象。该中间件在轻量级基于UDP代理的发布-订阅架构上扩展了感知专用服务，包括图像分片与重建、并发数据包传输、优先级感知调度和图像质量评估。该中间件在模拟UAV集群的异构硬件测试床上使用YOLOv8n目标检测进行评估。实验结果表明其端到端应用时延低、吞吐量显著高于轻量级UDP代理、在背景负载增加时能有效优先处理感知流量，并通过中间件级图像质量评估缓解目标检测性能退化。本工作为将AI特定数据处理集成到通信中间件中提供了一个初步框架，以支撑多智能体移动信息物理系统中新兴的分布式AI应用。

reserve_papers.title: Radar2Plan: Benchmarking 4D Radar for End-to-End Open-Loop Ego-Trajectory Planning
reserve_papers.abstract: Adverse weather and poor illumination remain major challenges for robust ego-trajectory planning in mobile autonomy. 4D radar offers reliable sensing under adverse conditions and direct radial-velocity measurements. However, sensing robustness does not necessarily translate into robust downstream planning, while existing 4D radar benchmarks focus primarily on perception rather than trajectory planning. We present Radar2Plan, a modular benchmark for open-loop ego-trajectory planning using real-world 4D radar data. Radar2Plan connects sensor encoders, scene representations, and planning heads through common interfaces, enabling controlled comparisons between different sensor and planner configurations. Using DSERT-RoLL and MAN TruckScenes, we evaluated seven combinations of camera, 4D radar, and LiDAR in four representative planning baselines and 12 weather and illumination conditions under a unified protocol. To our knowledge, Radar2Plan is the first benchmark dedicated to evaluating real-world 4D radars for autonomous driving planning. Experiments show that 4D radar alone supports competitive ego-trajectory planning and robust performance under adverse conditions. Sensor-configuration comparisons further demonstrate its complementary value to other modalities, while revealing dependencies on sensor combination and planning architecture. The modular design also supports additional datasets, sensing modalities, and planners, providing a flexible foundation for future research on radar-based autonomous driving planning.

reserve_papers.title: Real-Time Edge AI Camera-Radar Fusion for MOT with YOLOv11 and ByteTrack
reserve_papers.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning Technologies (ICMLT)
reserve_papers.abstract: Multi-sensor data fusion (MSDF) is a critical research area for Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and Autonomous Driving. By combining data from complementary sensors such as cameras, radars, and LiDARs, fusion techniques overcome the inherent limitations of individual sensors, significantly reducing uncertainty and increasing perception reliability. This paper focused on a novel, real-time multi-sensor data fusion (MSDF) architecture that collectively optimizes object detection, tracking, and multi-sensor consistent information for ADAS algorithms. In this approach, a YOLOv11n is deployed on a high-performance Hailo AI (8L) accelerator for camera-based detection. The detected results are processed through the ByteTrack algorithm for object tracking, and a K-MD7 24GHz Radar with built-in object tracking is also deployed to track object information. The collected camera and radar data are processed through a tightly coupled fusion module that performs association via the Hungarian algorithm and uses the Maximum Likelihood Estimation(MLE) for state estimation. This coordinated combination of a high-speed vision pipeline and precise radar measurements produces a markedly more robust and consistent perception output compared to single-sensor approaches.

reserve_papers.title: Graph Learning-Driven Multi-Vessel Association: Fusing Multimodal Data for Maritime Intelligence
reserve_papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
reserve_papers.abstract: Ensuring maritime safety and optimizing traffic management in increasingly crowded and complex waterways require effective waterway monitoring. However, current methods struggle with challenges arising from multimodal data, such as dimensional disparities, mismatched target counts, vessel scale variations, occlusions, and asynchronous data streams from systems like the automatic identification system (AIS) and closed-circuit television (CCTV). Traditional multi-vessel association methods often struggle with these complexities, particularly in densely trafficked waterways. To overcome these issues, we propose a graph learning-driven multi-vessel association (named GMvA) method tailored for maritime multimodal data fusion. By integrating AIS and CCTV data, GMvA leverages time series learning and graph neural networks to capture the spatiotemporal features of vessel trajectories effectively. To enhance feature representation, the proposed method incorporates temporal graph attention and spatiotemporal attention, effectively capturing both local and global vessel interactions. Furthermore, a multi-layer perceptron-based uncertainty fusion module computes robust similarity scores, and the Hungarian algorithm is adopted to ensure globally consistent and accurate target matching. To validate the efficacy of our method, we have also constructed a new maritime multimodal dataset (termed MaritimeMmD) for data fusion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GMvA delivers superior accuracy and robustness in multi-vessel association, outperforming existing methods even in challenging scenarios with high vessel density and incomplete or unevenly distributed AIS and CCTV data. The source dataset and code are available athttps://github.com/LouisYxLu/GMvA

reserve_papers.title: calibfusion: Transformer-Based Differentiable Calibration for Radar-Camera Fusion Detection in Water-Surface Environments
reserve_papers.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) Radar--Camera fusion improves perception under adverse illumination and weather, but its performance is sensitive to Radar--Camera extrinsic calibration: residual misalignment biases Radar-to-image projection and degrades cross-modal aggregation for downstream 2D detection. Existing calibration and auto-calibration methods are mainly developed for road and urban scenes with abundant structures and object constraints, whereas water-surface environments feature large textureless regions, sparse and intermittent targets, and wave-/specular-induced Radar clutter, which weakens explicit object-centric matching. We propose CalibFusion, a calibration-conditioned Radar--Camera fusion detector that learns implicit extrinsic refinement end-to-end with the detection objective. CalibFusion builds a multi-frame persistence-aware Radar density representation with intensity weighting and Doppler-guided suppression of fast-varying clutter. A cross-modal transformer interaction module predicts a confidence-gated refinement of the initial extrinsics, which is integrated through a differentiable projection-and-splatting operator to generate calibration-conditioned image-plane Radar features. Experiments on WaterScenes and FLOW show improved fusion-based 2D detection and robustness under synthetic miscalibration, supported by sensitivity analyses and qualitative Radar-to-image overlays. Results on nuScenes indicate that the refinement mechanism transfers beyond water-surface scenarios.

reserve_papers.title: Towards Accurate 3D Object Detection in Adverse Weather by Leveraging 4D Radar for LiDAR Geometry Enhancement
reserve_papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reserve_papers.abstract: 3D object detection is a critical component of autonomous driving, yet its performance degrades severely in adverse weather due to the degradation of LiDAR point clouds. While existing LiDAR-4D radar fusion methods enhance robustness by incorporating weather-robust 4D radar data, they often depend on well geometric structures from LiDAR and so struggle to effectively exploit radar data in case of degraded LiDAR data. To tackle this challenge, we propose REL, a novel 4D radar-guided LiDAR geometric enhancement framework. It utilizes 4D radar features to dynamically generate virtual LiDAR points, effectively increasing the density of degraded LiDAR data. Moreover, a Position-Guided Cross Attention (PGCA) module is proposed to enhance the feature representation of virtual points, while an Adaptive Feature Fusion (AFF) module is designed to integrate virtual and real LiDAR features. Extensive experiments on the K-Radar and Vod-Fog datasets demonstrate that REL achieves state-of-the-art 3D object detection performance under diverse adverse weather conditions. Notably, REL improves the overall AP3D by 9.3% on K-Radar and boosts the cyclist class by up to 52.9% 3D mAP under the most severe foggy condition on Vod-Fog.

reserve_papers.title: Do Pretrained Backbones Transfer to Physical Sensors? A Systematic Study of Multimodal Initialization Across the Sensor Stack
reserve_papers.abstract: Transfer learning from pretrained backbones has become standard practice in multi-sensor computer vision---yet two questions remain open: which pretrained weights transfer best to multi-sensor setups, and can in-domain pretraining outperform off-the-shelf solutions? Frameworks like MultiMAE demonstrate the utility of masked autoencoding in a multi-modal context, but rely entirely on dense, model-derived modalities. It is unclear how robustly these methods translate to real-world applications that use physical sensors, where the aggregation of diverse public datasets for large-scale pretraining inherently introduces modality sparsity. To investigate this systematically, we curate a multi-sensor autonomous driving collection of $2.82M$ images from 16 publicly available datasets, incorporating both physical hardware modalities (RGB, LWIR, NIR, Event) and model-derived modalities (Stereo Depth, Segmentation). We use this collection for in-domain pretraining based on the MultiMAE approach. We adapt MultiMAE's loss formulation to accommodate sparse samples, and study the effect of an enforced encoder bottleneck for modality alignment and of additional losses specific to dense reconstruction (SSIM and FFT). We then systematically compare against common pretrained backbones (ViT, MAE, DINO and MultiMAE) across downstream sensor fusion tasks. We find that MultiMAE is a surprisingly strong out-of-the-box baseline, transferring effectively even to modalities it has never seen, while our targeted modifications yield incremental but consistent improvements on multi-sensor transfer and overall robustness.

reserve_papers.abstract_zh: 从预训练骨干网络进行迁移学习已成为多传感器计算机视觉中的标准做法——然而两个问题仍未解决：哪些预训练权重最适合迁移到多传感器设置，以及域内预训练能否超越现成方案？像MultiMAE这样的框架展示了掩码自编码在多模态语境中的效用，但完全依赖稠密的、模型导出的模态。目前尚不清楚这些方法能多稳健地迁移到使用物理传感器的真实应用中，在这些应用中，为大规模预训练而聚合多样化的公开数据集会固有地引入模态稀疏性。为系统研究这一问题，我们整理了一个多传感器自动驾驶数据集，包含来自16个公开数据集的$2.82M$张图像，涵盖物理硬件模态（RGB、LWIR、NIR、Event）和模型导出模态（立体深度、分割）。我们使用该数据集基于MultiMAE方法进行域内预训练。我们调整MultiMAE的损失公式以适应稀疏样本，并研究强制编码器瓶颈对模态对齐的影响以及针对稠密重建的额外损失（SSIM和FFT）的影响。然后，我们在下游传感器融合任务中系统性地与常见预训练骨干网络（ViT、MAE、DINO和MultiMAE）进行比较。我们发现，MultiMAE是一个出乎意料的强大开箱即用基线，即使对从未见过的模态也能有效迁移，而我们针对性的修改在多传感器迁移和整体鲁棒性上带来了渐进但一致的改进。

reserve_papers.title: CLLAP: Contrastive Learning-based LiDAR-Augmented Pretraining for Enhanced Radar-Camera Fusion
reserve_papers.abstract: Accurate 3D object detection is critical for autonomous driving, necessitating reliable, cost-effective sensors capable of operating in adverse weather conditions. Camera and millimeter-wave radar fusion has emerged as a promising solution; however, these methods often rely on finely annotated radar data, which is scarce and labor-intensive to produce. To address this challenge, we present CLLAP, a Contrastive Learning-based LiDAR-Augmented Pretraining framework that enhances the performance of existing radar-camera fusion methods for 3D object detection. CLLAP leverages abundant LiDAR data to generate pseudo-radar data using the proposed L2R (LiDAR-to-Radar) Sampling method. Then, it incorporates this data into a novel dual-stage, dual-modality contrastive learning strategy, enabling effective self-supervised learning from paired pseudo-radar and image data. This approach facilitates effective pretraining of existing radar-camera fusion models in a plug-and-play manner, enhancing their feature extraction capabilities and improving detection accuracy and robustness. Experimental results using NuScenes and Lyft Level 5 datasets demonstrate significant performance improvements across three baseline models, highlighting CLLAP's effectiveness in advancing radar-camera fusion for autonomous driving applications.

reserve_papers.summary_zh: 论文提出CLLAP预训练框架，用LiDAR生成伪雷达数据并结合双阶段双模态对比学习，提升现有雷达-相机融合3D检测模型的性能与鲁棒性。
reserve_papers.migration_zh: 研究推断：可将L2R采样生成伪Radar与双阶段对比预训练迁移至Radar–AIS或视觉–AIS关联，在融合编码器前以伪模态输入和无标注对齐监督增强特征，并调整双分支对比结构。
reserve_papers.abstract_zh: 准确的3D目标检测对自动驾驶至关重要，需要可靠、低成本且能在恶劣天气条件下工作的传感器。相机与毫米波雷达融合已成为一种有前景的解决方案；然而，这些方法通常依赖精细标注的雷达数据，而此类数据稀缺且标注劳动强度大。为应对这一挑战，我们提出CLLAP，一种基于对比学习的LiDAR增强预训练框架，可提升现有雷达-相机融合方法在3D目标检测中的性能。CLLAP利用丰富的LiDAR数据，通过所提出的L2R（LiDAR-to-Radar）采样方法生成伪雷达数据。然后，它将这些数据纳入一种新颖的双阶段、双模态对比学习策略，从而能够从配对的伪雷达与图像数据中进行有效的自监督学习。该方法以即插即用的方式促进现有雷达-相机融合模型的有效预训练，增强其特征提取能力并提高检测精度与鲁棒性。使用NuScenes和Lyft Level 5数据集的实验结果表明，三个基线模型均取得显著的性能提升，凸显了CLLAP在推进自动驾驶雷达-相机融合方面的有效性。

reserve_papers.title: ATN3D: Density-Aware LiDAR-Radar Early 3D Object Detection Under Extreme Sparsity
reserve_papers.abstract: 3D object detection is the backbone of perception for automated vehicles (AV) and broader intelligent transportation systems applications. Long-range detection is challenging because sensing evidence is sparse; yet this ``long-range'' scenario is routine in traffic. Although >30m is often labeled long-range in computer vision, on roadways it affords only approx. 1-2s for perception and decision-making. Under such extreme sparsity, two core challenges arise. First, early multimodal fusion tends to discard sparsity information and inject noise from empty or falsely occupied cells, degrading long-range recall. Second, context-agnostic uniform channel supervision favors dense and near-range samples, leaving far and small objects under-optimized, delaying the earliest detection of distant objects. We propose ``Ask The Neighbor'' (ATN3D), a LiDAR-Radar framework tailored for sparse-range conditions. ATN3D introduces (i) Density-aware early fusion with cross-modal gating that conditions fusion on per-voxel density/sparsity and Radar evidence, (ii) Occupancy-gated neighborhood aggregation with circular kernels to aggregate only from credible cells, (iii) Evidence-conditioned channel self-attention to adapt channel weights with weather/range, and (iv) a Range-aware loss that re-balances classification and localization by distance, aligning training with distance-stratified evaluation. On the VoD benchmark across clear and foggy conditions, ATN3D surpasses strong baselines: +3.55% mAP in clear weather and +8.41% mAP under simulated heavy fog; for >30m objects, gains are +3.33% (clear) and +2.09% (heavy fog). These results indicate earlier and more reliable long-range detections under sparse sensing in on-road traffic.
reserve_papers.reason: 陆上多传感器稀疏融合检测，提供密度感知门控与可信邻域聚合，可迁移至雷达/视觉多传感器检测，但无海事场景。
reserve_papers.summary_zh: 针对极端稀疏条件下远距离3D目标检测中早期融合丢失稀疏信息、均匀监督偏袒近距密集样本的问题，提出密度感知的LiDAR-Radar早期融合框架ATN3D，在VoD数据集雾天和晴天均提升mAP与远距召回。
reserve_papers.migration_zh: 研究推断：可将密度感知跨模态门控与占用门控邻域聚合迁移至Radar–AIS或视觉–AIS关联前端，以体素/单元稀疏度与可信证据为门控输入，保留远距小目标特征并抑制空单元噪声。
reserve_papers.abstract_zh: 3D目标检测是自动驾驶汽车（AV）及更广泛智能交通系统应用感知的骨干。远距离检测具有挑战性，因为传感证据稀疏；然而这种“远距离”场景在交通中是常态。尽管在计算机视觉中超过30m常被标为远距离，在道路上它仅提供约1-2s的感知与决策时间。在这种极端稀疏下，出现两个核心挑战。第一，早期多模态融合倾向于丢弃稀疏信息，并从空或虚假占用单元注入噪声，降低远距离召回。第二，上下文无关的均匀通道监督偏向密集和近距样本，使远距和小目标优化不足，延迟对远处目标的最早检测。我们提出“Ask The Neighbor”（ATN3D），一个面向稀疏距离条件的LiDAR-Radar框架。ATN3D引入（i）密度感知早期融合与跨模态门控，以逐体素密度/稀疏度和Radar证据为条件进行融合，（ii）占用门控邻域聚合与圆形核，仅从可信单元聚合，（iii）证据条件通道自注意力，随天气/距离自适应通道权重，以及（iv）距离感知损失，按距离重新平衡分类与定位，使训练与距离分层评估对齐。在VoD基准的晴天和雾天条件下，ATN3D超越强基线：晴天mAP +3.55%，模拟浓雾下mAP +8.41%；对于>30m目标，增益为+3.33%（晴天）和+2.09%（浓雾）。这些结果表明在道路上稀疏传感下更早、更可靠的远距离检测。
